lead: New (21 October 2026): Core review 2, after the third run of the queue. Three prompts are ready again: the people trial R7c-1 (pull request #539 now writes the per-guide soleRow field that run 4 stopped on; run 5), the narrow depot C35a (the doorway notch that failed all twelve attempts was the prompt's own fault: the blockout's doorways now read solid and the prompt says to paint them opaque; all four views, three new attempts each) and the hydro plant C29a (a new prompt: a brick turbine house with one tall arched window, a penstock from a small intake chamber and a tailrace arch, painted r0 to r3 over Core's new Blender blockout, strict tests). Core's decisions and the re-test of the twelve depot attempts are in codex-queue/status/CORE-REVIEW-2.md on branch claude/codex-queue.

New (21 October 2026): the textured pilot, TB1, the first group below. Core built the warehouse, the water pump and the power plant as clean Blender blockouts matched to their painted r0, projected the original painting onto them and rendered r0 to r3 at the game's exact camera with the game's sun (branch claude/art-scaffolds-review-2, assets/source/buildings-v2/scaffolds-textured/, head eef723cf). The author found that texture "a bit fallen apart" (cloned and smeared patches, seams, blocky chimney backs, smeared pipes), so TB1 asks Codex to repaint every view over its textured render into one coherent painting in the style of the original r0, keeping the render's silhouette, camera, proportions and light. Twelve pictures, at most three attempts each, with stricter tests than the scaffold prompts (IoU 0.92, 95th percentile 16 and maximum 32 canvas px, height within 8 per cent). New lane art/textured-pilot, created from develop by Codex; nothing else of the queue changes.

Core review 1 (21 October 2026), the second run of the queue. The boundary test of the scaffold prompts is now a distribution: the 95th percentile of the boundary distances at most 3 game px AND the largest distance at most 6 game px (the old rule took the largest distance alone and refused good pictures for one thin protrusion). The scaffold's geometry wins: parts the lit scaffold shows are painted as shown, whatever a prompt says about a hidden front. Each prompt starts with a CORE REVIEW 1 header that says so.

Done and accepted (not on this page any more): Big Station, Big Farm Halt, Town hall and Warehouse (all twelve views) and the windmill body r0. Core's decisions on every refused attempt are in codex-queue/status/CORE-REVIEW-1.md on branch claude/codex-queue.

Each group below is ONE Codex conversation: paste its prompts one after another, each after the previous one finishes. The button Copy whole conversation copies the group's prompts in order, with a separator line between them; Copy prompt copies a single one.

Codex works in the main checkout (G:DEVTerepasztal	erepasztal), which has one branch checked out at a time. So run ONE group at a time there. Two groups can run at the same time only if Codex gives each its own git worktree. Every group is on its own branch, except that the Later prompt C33b belongs to the Rotations conversation (same branch, art/535-rotations).

Turned views are painted over Core's 3D scaffolds (branch claude/art-scaffolds-review-2, head fc07d589); each prompt says how to read them. The narrow depot (C35a) and the hydro plant (C29a) have Core-made Blender blockouts (branch claude/art-scaffolds-review-2, f44a8b9e). Accepted pictures are not painted again.

The branch already holds twelve jobs from 19 October: each prompt rebases before it pushes.
